# Results — Study 384 (ISM-PMI-Regime)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folklore — **"only own
stocks when the manufacturing PMI is above 50"** — tested on a **transparent PMI proxy**.
The true ISM Manufacturing PMI is a proprietary survey and the free FRED fallback
(`NAPM` / regional-Fed diffusion indices) is unreachable from this environment, so we
construct the PMI from a fixed 37-name industrial/manufacturing basket: each month's
**diffusion index** is the share of names with positive 3-month momentum, on a PMI-like
0–100 axis (smoothed with a 3-month EMA), and **> 50** is the "expansion" regime. We then
compare next-month SPY returns by regime and run a deployable above-50 timing rule.
Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — SPY + a fixed 37-name industrial basket (public, no key) |
| Window | 1995-04-30 → 2026-06-30 (**375** month-ends; **31.2** years) |
| PMI proxy | monthly diffusion index of the basket (share with positive 3-month momentum × 100, 3-month EMA); **PROXY** for ISM Manufacturing PMI |
| Regime | proxy **> 50** = expansion (own stocks), **≤ 50** = contraction (cash) |
| Above-50 share | the proxy reads above 50 in **71.7%** of months (manufacturing expands most of the time) |
| Entry / costs | 1-month execution lag (PMI of month *t* acted on in *t+1*); one-way 10 bps per regime switch |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** A 37-name surviving-large-cap industrial
> basket is a *noisier, narrower* diffusion gauge than the ISM survey's hundreds of
> purchasing managers, and it carries **survivorship** (breadth-of-the-survivors runs
> mildly bullish). The verdict does **not** hinge on the proxy matching the survey
> month-for-month: it hinges on the fact that the above-50 regime's *return* edge over the
> unconditional mean is **absent** on this tape — which is what the macro literature
> already predicts (PMI is a coincident growth gauge, not a return-timing signal).

## The signal — next-month SPY returns by PMI regime

1-month execution lag; the unconditional column is *all* monthly returns over the same
tape (the honest base rate). Welch *t* compares the above-50 mean to the below-50 mean; the
placebo *p* is the share of 20,000 block-resampled regime labellings whose above-minus-below
spread **matches or beats** the real one.

| regime | n months | mean monthly | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **PMI > 50** (expansion) | 268 | **+0.958%** | 66% |
| **PMI ≤ 50** (contraction) | 106 | **+0.962%** | 63% |
| unconditional (base rate) | 374 | +0.959% | 65% |

| above-minus-below spread | Welch *t* | block-placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **−0.004% / month** | **−0.01** | 0.491 |

Read it carefully. The above-50 monthly mean (**+0.958%**) and the below-50 mean
(**+0.962%**) are **the same number** — the regime spread is **−0.004%/month**, with
**Welch t = −0.01** and a **block-placebo p = 0.49** (a coin matches it half the time).
On this proxy, sorting SPY's forward return by whether manufacturing is "expanding" buys
you **nothing**: the market drifts up at essentially the same rate in both regimes. The
"PMI works" story is the unconditional up-drift plus the fact that PMI sits above 50
**72%** of the time anyway — *own-stocks-above-50 is, to the basis point, own-stocks.*

## The deployable rule — own SPY only above 50, else cash

Hold SPY when last month's proxy was above 50, else cash (0% yield); 1-month lag; 10 bps
one-way on each of the **57** regime switches. Gross/net of cost, vs plain buy-and-hold.

| book | ann. return | ann. vol | Sharpe | max drawdown | final wealth (1995→2026) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| timing (net @10 bps) | **+8.06%** | 10.4% | **0.77** | **−40.8%** | **10.3×** |
| buy-and-hold | +11.51% | 15.1% | 0.76 | −50.8% | **24.9×** |

The timing rule's Sharpe (**0.77**) essentially **ties** buy-and-hold's (**0.76**) — the
one real thing it does is trim the worst drawdown (−41% vs −51%) by sitting in cash ~28% of
the time. But it pays for that comfort dearly: it forfeits **more than half the terminal
wealth** (10.3× vs 24.9×) and **3.5 points of annual return**. That is not an edge — it is
**less beta**. A risk-matched comparison (lever the timing book to 15% vol, or simply hold
72% equities) recovers the same Sharpe with none of the regime machinery.

## Robustness — flat across the threshold

| threshold | n above | n below | spread / month | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 45 | 285 | 89 | +0.187% | +0.26 | 0.349 |
| **50** (folklore) | 268 | 106 | **−0.004%** | **−0.01** | 0.491 |
| 55 | 248 | 126 | +0.351% | +0.63 | 0.220 |

No threshold from 45 to 55 produces a spread anywhere near significance; the largest *t* is
0.63. There is no cut-point at which "PMI regime" becomes a return-timing signal.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic PMI-like regime series (persistent AR(1) cycle around 50) with an SPY-like
price whose monthly drift is lifted **only in above-50 months** by a *known* edge:

| planted edge (per month, above-50 only) | above mean | below mean | spread | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **+0.00%** (no edge) | +0.798% | +0.978% | −0.180% | **−0.58** | 0.717 |
| **+1.50%** (large edge) | +2.105% | +1.221% | +0.884% | **+2.86** | **0.003** |

With **no** planted edge the test stays well below t = 2 (it does not manufacture a regime
signal from noise). Only a **large** planted edge — +1.5%/month, enormous — drives t to 2.86
and p to 0.003. The control proves the measurement engine is unbiased *and* powered: a real
regime edge of plausible size *would* show up. On the real tape it does not, because there
isn't one.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The above-50 / below-50 monthly-return spread is **−0.004%** at
  **Welch t = −0.01** (placebo p = 0.49) and never clears t = 0.6 at any threshold from 45
  to 55. The PMI's 50 line carries **no** return-timing information on this proxy — exactly
  what the macro literature implies (PMI is a *coincident* growth diffusion index, not a
  forward equity-return signal). Proxy/literature framing cannot upgrade a t ≈ 0 ⇒ **NONE**.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The above-50 timing rule **ties** buy-and-hold on Sharpe
  (0.77 vs 0.76) while forfeiting **half the terminal wealth** (10.3× vs 24.9×) and 3.5
  points/yr. Its only effect is **less market exposure** — it trims drawdown the way any
  cash-heavy allocation does. Risk-matched, the edge vanishes: it is beta you de-risked, not
  alpha you found.
- **"Free regime-timing lunch"? — BUSTED.** "Stay out below 50, ride the expansion above
  it" sounds like avoiding the bad regime for free. But the bad regime's *returns* aren't
  bad (below-50 months average +0.96%, same as above-50), so stepping out of them just
  removes good up-drift. The lunch is paid for in forgone compounding.
